name: Precision screwdriver set
description: Small screwdrivers with swappable tips, in the tiny sizes and shapes that phones use.
usedFor: Removing the small screws inside a phone.
caution: Use the tip that fits exactly. The wrong tip ruins the screw head.

name: Plastic opening picks
description: Thin, flexible plastic triangles that slide into the seam of a phone.
usedFor: Cutting through adhesive and holding a seam open.
caution: Insert only a few millimeters. Cables and the battery can sit right at the edge.

name: Plastic spudger
description: A plastic stick with a flat end, made for gentle prying.
usedFor: Lifting connectors and easing parts apart.
caution: Lift connectors straight up from their edges.

name: Suction cup
description: A small cup with a handle that grips smooth glass.
usedFor: Lifting a screen or glass back to open the first small gap.
caution: Pull gently. If the glass is cracked, cover it with tape first so the cup can grip.

name: ESD-safe tweezers
description: Fine-tipped tweezers made so they do not pass static to parts.
usedFor: Holding small screws, brackets and cables.
caution: Do not touch connector pins or the battery with metal tips.

name: Heat pad or heat gun
description: A heat source used on its lowest setting to soften adhesive.
usedFor: Warming the edges of a glued back or screen.
caution: Keep the heat moving and on the edges. Stop when the surface is too hot to keep a finger on.

name: Isopropyl alcohol, 90% or stronger
description: A cleaning alcohol that dries quickly and leaves little behind.
usedFor: Loosening battery adhesive and cleaning away old glue.
caution: It is flammable. Keep it away from heat tools, and let it dry fully.

name: Screw tray or mat
description: A tray with sections, or a marked mat, for laying out parts in order.
usedFor: Keeping every screw matched to the place it came from.
caution: Screws differ in length. A long one in the wrong hole can pierce the board.

name: Anti-static mat
description: A work surface that safely drains static electricity away.
usedFor: Giving the phone and loose parts a safe place to rest.
caution: Connect it to ground, or it gives much less protection.

name: Anti-static wrist strap
description: A band on your wrist, joined by a wire to a ground point.
usedFor: Keeping your body free of static while you handle boards.
caution: The strap should touch your skin, and its clip must be connected to ground.

name: Soft brush
description: A small brush with soft, non-metal bristles.
usedFor: Cleaning lint and dust out of ports and off boards.
caution: Never clean a port with a pin, needle or other metal object.

name: Clear packing tape
usedFor: Holding cracked glass together during a repair.
caution: Cover every crack, and still wear gloves.

name: Safety glasses
description: Clear glasses that protect your eyes from flying pieces.
usedFor: Every repair, especially around glass and springs.
caution: Regular eyeglasses are not enough protection.

name: Cut-resistant gloves
description: Gloves that protect your hands from sharp edges.
usedFor: Handling cracked screens and glass backs.
caution: Take them off for delicate work with small connectors.

name: Metal container with dry sand
description: A fireproof place to put a battery that starts to fail.
usedFor: Keeping nearby whenever you remove a battery.
caution: Have it ready before you start, and only use it if you can do so safely.
